newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Israel in West Bank stalemate.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel in West Bank stalemate.

text.p: Israel will not go ahead with its planned withdrawal from a further nine percent of the West Bank if the Palestinian Authority (PA) refuses to cooperate, an Israeli official said.
The latest snag in troubled Middle East peace moves came as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu prepared to leave for a three-day visit to Russia starting on Monday.
Israel Radio said Israeli Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh and apparently Netanyahu's political adviser, Dore Gold, would not go to Moscow as planned because of problems with the Palestinian Authority.

"We have to give the area to somebody...It's up to them," the official, who asked not to be identified, told Reuters after Foreign Minister David Levy met top Palestinian negotiator Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen.
Abbas's team left immediately afterwards for the self-ruled Gaza Strip to consult Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
It gave Levy a written rejection of Israel's withdrawal plan, including a demand for Israel to freeze plans to build a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Palestinians regard the construction project as prejudicing negotiations on the city in final peace talks scheduled to start on March 17.
But Levy said he made clear that Israel would not reconsider the plan to build 6,500 homes for Jews in East Jerusalem nor negotiate the West Bank withdrawal.

"The government of Israel is operating according to the agreement," he told reporters after the two-hour meeting with Abbas. "They are going back to their chairman (Arafat). They must consult...and give us an answer."

Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said after meeting Arafat in Gaza that it was the Palestinians who were waiting for answers from Israel on negotiating the West Bank pullback and stopping settlement.
"I think we're waiting for an answer from Mr Netanyahu," he said. "We are also consulting and being in touch with the Arab leaders...The situation is much more in a crisis situation."

Levy, asked if the dispute over the West Bank pullout, which Israel had intended to implement this week, might delay the talks on a final peace deal, said: "I cannot say anything until I get their answer."
The Palestinians are furious that Israel unilaterally set the scope of the withdrawal, the first of three set out in a 1995 interim deal and reaffirmed in a January accord reached with Netanyahu.

Israel says a U.S. note attached to the January deal left the extent of the pullback to its sole discretion. But the Palestinians say the first redeployment should cover 30 percent of the West Bank areas still controlled by Israel.

"The danger surrounding us is forcing us to decide whether to be free and masters over our land or slaves of the Israelis," Ahmed Abdel Rahman, general-secretary of Arafat's cabinet, said in a fiery speech in Gaza.
"From now on, resisting settlements will not be through words, condemnation or complaints to the U.N. Security Council."
Levy cancelled a trip to the United States in order to maintain contacts with the Palestinians while Netanyahu is in Russia.
Netanyahu spent most of Sunday trying to quell a rebellion within his own government over the proposed withdrawal. Hawks in his coalition say Israel is giving up too much of the West Bank.
